artworks.title: Abduction of Chrysippus (Darius Painter)
artworks.description: Apulian volute-krater (Berlin): Laius' abduction of Chrysippus, the beautiful son of Pelops — South Italian vase-painting of the crime that precedes Thebes' curse. Not the Stoic philosopher of Soli.

artworks.title: Abduction of Chrysippus (detail)
artworks.description: Detail of the Berlin krater: Chrysippus seized — the Pelopid youth Hyginus says Laius carried from the Nemean games.

artworks.title: Abduction of Chrysippus (Baltimore Painter)
artworks.description: Apulian vase (Fiesole): another abduction of Chrysippus — the same Pelopid rape that vase-painters paired with underworld and bridal scenes.

artworks.title: Abduction of Chrysippus (Baltimore Painter, reverse angle)
artworks.description: Second view of the Fiesole Chrysippus abduction — Pelops' son as South Italian narrative pottery, centuries before Stoic Chrysippus of Soli borrowed the name.

popCulture.title: Chrysippus of Elis
popCulture.description: Son of Pelops, abducted by Laius and later killed by Atreus and Thyestes — the mythic Chrysippus, not Chrysippus of Soli the Stoic.

popCulture.title: Laius
popCulture.description: The Theban king whose abduction of Chrysippus is told as the first crime that shadows the house of Oedipus.
